title: Word Break
contract: Return whether s can be segmented into nonempty dictionary words, which may be reused. Empty s is segmentable.
optimal: Set<String> dict=new HashSet<>(Arrays.asList(words));boolean[] dp=new boolean[s.length()+1];dp[0]=true;for(int end=1;end<=s.length();end++){for(int start=0;start<end;start++)if(dp[start]&&dict.contains(s.substring(start,end))){dp[end]=true;break;}emit("Check a reachable prefix plus one dictionary word","prefix length",end,"reachable",dp);}return dp[s.length()];
reasoning: Try every word-ending boundary recursively; failures may revisit the same suffix repeatedly.
dp[end] records whether the prefix of that length can be segmented.

Only extend from reachable prefixes and do not accept an empty dictionary word as progress. Java substring allocation and hashing cost up to O(n), so this direct implementation has cubic worst-case character work.
complexity: Exponential boundary search, O(n²) live substring/stack upper bound
O(n³) character work, O(n+dictionary size) retained state
